newsitem.title: INDIA: Trade in India gilts to ease next fortnight-SBICAP.
newsitem.headline: Trade in India gilts to ease next fortnight-SBICAP.

text.p: Trades in Indian government securities will dwindle as the year-end approached, SBI Capital Markets (SBICAP) said in a debt market report on Monday.
"The year-end considerations will be a major dampener in the coming fortnight," SBICAP said.
The financial year ends on March 31.
SBICAP said it expected liquidity to tighten in the current fortnight as advance tax payments left the banking system.
It estimated the tax outflows to be around 50 billion rupees and said the temporary shortage on this count could lead to a hardening in call money rates to an average of 7.0 percent.
"Subscriptions to repo auctions would also fall as a result (of tighter liquidity) and trading activity will continue to be restricted to the shorter segment of the curve," SBICAP said.
The report added that it expected banks to maintain their current interest rates till after the announcement of the credit policy in April.
It said it expected the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to maintain yields at the treasury bill auctions despite market expectations and inflationary pressures.
"Secondary yields on treasury bills will shift upwards during the fortnight," SBICAP said.
"Yields on short-term gilts could also move upwards, while yield on medium and long term gilts will not move more because of lack of trading interest in that segment."
